title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: This document explains the EU regulation that sets common rules for AI and updates several existing laws, outlining how businesses must comply and what protections are put in place. It highlights the changes to other regulations and directives to ensure AI technology is safe, trustworthy and respects citizens’ rights across the EU.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government’s response to the 2020 report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards outlines its commitment to establish clear rules, promote transparency, and ensure AI is developed safely and ethically. It emphasizes collaboration with industry, research bodies, and international partners to create shared standards that protect public interests while encouraging innovation.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual will establish clear rules and oversight to manage how artificial intelligence is used in creating and assessing qualifications, ensuring fairness, reliability, and transparency. The policy aims to protect students and maintain public trust in exam systems while encouraging responsible AI innovation.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how AI systems use copyrighted works and assesses the effects of this practice on creators, consumers, and the broader industry. It provides recommendations to balance the benefits of AI innovation with the need to protect intellectual property rights.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a response to the House of Lords AI Select Committee report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining its strategy to address the risks and opportunities of artificial intelligence. It calls for stronger regulation, greater investment in AI research, workforce skills development, and international cooperation to keep the UK at the forefront of safe and responsible AI innovation.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document sets out the scope, purpose, and responsibilities of a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence relates to public standards. It also includes a FAQ section to explain key concepts, procedures, and expectations for the committee’s work.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the UK Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence. Their submission outlines key challenges and offers recommendations for improving AI regulation.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy examines how AI technologies will influence the regulation of medical products, highlighting both opportunities and challenges in ensuring safety and efficacy. It outlines steps for applying the AI White Paper principles to develop clear, consistent regulatory frameworks that protect patients while fostering innovation.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted and influential AI‑driven defence entity worldwide for its size, prioritising innovation, robust governance and ethical use of AI. It focuses on developing advanced AI capabilities, building strong partnerships, and ensuring secure, responsible deployment to maintain a strategic advantage.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport industry to harness AI benefits and address risks. It details strategies for safe, responsible AI adoption in transport services.
